newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures finish near session highs.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures finish near session highs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures finished sharply higher Thursday after breaking through resistance earlier in the session, industry sources said.
November ended the day-long rally up 16.6 cents at $2.346 per million British thermal units, just shy of the day's $2.355 high. December settled 16.7 cents higher at $2.531.

"We toyed with $2 today (Gulf cash). It was a wake-up call for buyers," said one futures trader. "We're finally at a price where people need more coverage," he added, noting the upcoming winter heating season.
The trader added the rally in the heating oil market may have added more psychological support to the contract.
Technically, support in November was pegged at $2.26, which had previously been an important resistance level. Further support was in the $2.16-2.165 area. Resistance was seen in the mid-$2.40s.

Cash prices on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes moved 10 cents higher early into the high-$1.90s to low-$2 range. Midcontinent prices hovered in the $1.85-1.88 area. At the New York city-gate, prices were in the low-to-mid $2.30s, while on the Appalachian pipes gas sold in the $2.15-2.20 area.
NYMEX said an estimated 40,159 Henry Hub contracts traded, up significantly from Wednesday's revised tally of 20,361. The 12-month strip jumped 8.5 cents to $2.20.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled 2.5 cents higher at $1.025. Physical prices held steady in the high-C$1.20s per gigajoule.
NYMEX November Permian natgas ended up 8.5 cents at $1.955. NYMEX said today's volume totalled six.
Physical gas traded in the basin in the $1.81-1.86 area.

Also near the highs of the day, KCBT's November contract settled 13 cents higher at $2.07. Deffereds were two to 10 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 3.6 cents to 27.6 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical prices at Waha climbed about two cents higher to the $1.86-1.88 area.
